cards.b: The number of live births per 1,000 people in a year.
The number of deaths per 1,000 people in a year.
Birth rate minus death rate. Positive is natural increase, negative is natural decrease.
The average number of children a woman has in her lifetime. About 2.1 is replacement level in HICs.
Deaths of children under one year old per 1,000 live births per year.

cards.f: Two reasons for high birth rates in LICs
cards.b: High infant mortality, so parents have more children; children work and support parents; little contraception.

cards.f: Two reasons for low birth rates in HICs
cards.b: Contraception widely available; women in education and careers; children are costly; low infant mortality.
Too many people for the resources available, so living standards are low or falling.
Too few people to make full use of the resources, so living standards could be higher.
The number of people that makes the best use of resources and gives the highest standard of living.
Wide base (high birth rate), steep narrowing with age (high death rate, low life expectancy).
Narrow base (low birth rate), wide top (long life expectancy), more women than men at the top.
People aged under 15 and over 64, who rely on the working-age population (15 to 64).
Anti-natalist policies reduce the birth rate; pro-natalist policies encourage more births.
Started 1979; changed to two children 2016, three in 2021. Fertility fell, but ageing, 4-2-1 problem and more males than females.

short.q: Explain why infant mortality is linked to high birth rates.
short.model: Where many babies die, parents have more children to make sure some survive to adulthood. This keeps the birth rate high.
points: high infant mortality leads parents to have more children
so some survive to support the family/work

short.q: Describe the features of an ageing population pyramid.
short.model: It has a narrow base showing a low birth rate and a wide top showing high life expectancy. There are more women than men in the oldest age groups.

short.q: Explain why an ageing population is a problem for a government.
short.model: There are fewer workers paying tax but more elderly needing pensions and healthcare. This raises costs and may lead to labour shortages.

short.q: Explain why overpopulation is about resources, not just numbers.
short.model: A country is overpopulated when it has too many people for its resources and technology, so living standards fall. A densely populated rich country may not be overpopulated.
points: valid contrast (e.g. rich, dense country not overpopulated)

short.q: Explain one success and one problem of a named population policy.
short.model: China's one-child policy cut the fertility rate from about 5.8 to about 1.6, easing pressure on resources. However, it created an ageing population with fewer workers.
points: named policy with a valid success
